'''Stuart Leonard Pimm''' (born 27 February 1949) is the Doris Duke Chair of [[Conservation Ecology]] at [[Duke University]]. His early career was as a theoretical ecologist but he now specializes in scientific research of [[biodiversity]] and [[conservation biology]].<ref name="n1">{{Cite journal |last1=Pimm |first1=S. == Education ==
Pimm was born in [[Derbyshire]], United Kingdom. He was educated at the [[University of Oxford]] and was awarded a [[PhD]] in [[Ecology]] from [[New Mexico State University]] in 1974.<ref name="pimmphd">{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Stuart |last=Pimm |title=Community Process and Structure |publisher=[[New Mexico State University]] |date=1974 |author-link=Stuart Pimm |id={{ProQuest|302713548}}}}</ref>

== Research ==
Pimm is currently Doris Duke Chair of Conservation Ecology in the [[Nicholas School of the Environment]] at [[Duke University]], [[Durham, North Carolina|Durham]], [[North Carolina]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nicholas School Faculty, Stuart L. Pimm |url=https://nicholas.duke.edu/people/faculty/pimm |access-date=2010-11-18 |publisher=[[Duke University]]}}</ref> Pimm has collaborated with a wide range of other scientists, including [[Robert May, Baron May of Oxford|Robert May]],<ref name="may">{{Cite journal |last1=Sugihara |first1=G. |author1-link=George Sugihara |last2=Bersier |first2=L. F. |last3=Southwood |first3=T. R. |last4=Pimm |first4=S. L. |author4-link=Stuart Pimm |last5=May |first5=R. M. |author5-link=Robert May, Baron May of Oxford |title=Predicted correspondence between species abundances and dendrograms of niche similarities |doi=10.1073/pnas.0831096100 |journal=[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences]] |volume=100 |issue=9 |pages=5246–5251 |year=2003 |pmid=12702773 |pmc=154330 |bibcode=2003PNAS..100.5246S |doi-access=free}}</ref> [[Peter H. Raven]], [[Joel E. Cohen]], [[George Sugihara]], [[Thomas Lovejoy]], and [[Jared Diamond]]. His early work has examined the mathematical properties of [[food web]]s and indicated that complex food webs should be less stable than simple food webs.<ref name=Pimm>{{cite book |author=Pimm, Stuart L. |title=Food webs |publisher=University of Chicago Press |location=Chicago |year=2002 |isbn=0-226-66832-0 }}</ref> Since 1990s, he concentrated on the patterns of species extinctions, the rate of species extinction and practical methods to stop them.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Pimm |first1=S. L. |last2=Jenkins |first2=C. N. |last3=Abell |first3=R. |last4=Brooks |first4=T. M. |last5=Gittleman |first5=J. L. |last6=Joppa |first6=L. N. |last7=Raven |first7=P. H. |last8=Roberts |first8=C. == Awards ==
He is an acknowledged authority in the field of conservation biology, recognized with several awards:

* World Sustainability Award (2025)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Stuart Pimm {{!}} World Sustainability Award {{!}} MDPI Sustainability Foundation |url=https://mdpi-foundation.org/award/awardees/prof-dr-stuart-pimm |access-date=2025-10-06 |website=mdpi-foundation.org}}</ref>
* [[International Cosmos Prize]] (2019).<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-11-25 |title=Stuart Pimm Receives International Prize |url=https://nicholas.duke.edu/news/stuart-pimm-receives-international-prize |access-date=2023-06-06 |website=Nicholas School of the Environment |language=en}}</ref>
* [[Tyler Prize for Environmental Achievement]] (2010).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Past Laureates |url=https://tylerprize.org/laureates/past-laureates/ |access-date=2023-06-06 |website=Tyler Prize for Environmental Achievement |language=en-US}}</ref>
* Dr. A. H. [[Heineken Prizes|Heineken Prize from the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (2006).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Altena |first=Trijntje van |title=Stuart L. Pimm |url=https://www.heinekenprizes.org/portfolio-items/stuart-l-pimm/ |access-date=2023-06-06 |website=Heineken Prizes |language=en-US}}</ref>
* Edward T. LaRoe III Memorial Award from the [[Society for Conservation Biology|Society of Conservation Biology]] (2006).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Society for Conservation Biology {{!}} Past Recipients |url=https://conbio.org/professional-development/service-awards/past-recipients/ |access-date=2023-06-06 |website=conbio.org}}</ref>
* Marsh Prize for Conservation from the [[Zoological Society of London]] (2003).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Marsh Charitable Trust – Marsh Award for Conservation Biology |url=https://www.marshcharitabletrust.org/award/marsh-award-for-conservation-biology/ |access-date=2023-06-06 |website=www.marshcharitabletrust.org}}</ref>

New Mexico State University made him an alumnus of the year in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Archive {{!}} New Mexico State University Alumni |url=https://www.nmsualumni.org/archive.html |access-date=2023-06-06 |website=www.nmsualumni.org}}</ref> A new wasp species from the cloud forests of [[Colombia]]'s tropical [[Andes]] has been named ''[[Dolichomitus pimmi]]'' in honor of Pimm and his conservation efforts in that region.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nicholas.duke.edu/news/newly-discovered-wasp-species-named-honor-duke-conservation-scientist-stuart-pimm |title=Newly Discovered Wasp Species Named to Honor Duke Conservation Scientist Stuart Pimm |publisher=Duke Nicholas School of the Environment |date=2020-06-04 |access-date=2020-07-02}}</ref>

== SavingSpecies and Saving Nature ==
In 2010, Pimm founded a non-profit organization called SavingSpecies to preserve and restore natural habitats. In 2019, the organization was dissolved and Saving Nature was created to reflect a broader mission from the work that Saving Species has started.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.guidestar.org/profile/45-3868475 |title=Guidestar: SavingSpecies |publisher=Guidestar |date=2020-05-19 |access-date=2020-05-19}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://savingnature.com/ |title=Saving Nature |publisher=Saving Nature |date=2020-09-26 |access-date=2020-09-26}}</ref> Saving Nature partners with local nonprofit organizations to connect fragmented habitats into biocorridors for wildlife. It works in biodiversity hotspots, such as in [[Colombia]], [[Brazil]], [[Ecuador]], [[India]], [[Indonesia]] and [[Tanzania]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-06-15 |title=Mazariegos & Pimm: Animals in Western Andes Can Finally Find a Date |url=https://veronikaperkova.com/2021/06/15/mazariegos-pimm/ |access-date=2023-06-07 |website=VERONIKA PERKOVÁ |language=en-US}}</ref> In [[Colombia]], Pimm has worked with local organizations, on projects linking fragmented forests, including expansion of the La Mesenia - Paramillo Nature Reserve.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Recognized as one of the world's most biodiverse regions |first=the tropical Andes host more than 10% of the planet's biodiversity-roughly two million species of plants |last2=This precious ecosystem is in peril because |first2=in the past few decades |last3=La Mesenia-Paramillo Nature Reserve in the Colombian Andes is attempting to stave off the threat by restoring 3 |first3=500 hectares (8 |date=2021-07-02 |title=In the Colombian Andes, a forest corridor staves off species extinction |url=https://news.mongabay.com/2021/07/in-the-colombian-andes-a-forest-corridor-staves-off-species-extinction/ |access-date=2025-10-06 |website=Mongabay Environmental News |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Controversy==
In 2014, Pimm was involved in a controversy related to allegedly sexist remarks he made in a [[book review]] published by the [[Elsevier]] journal [[Biological Conservation (journal)|Biological Conservation]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pimm |first1=Stuart |date=December 2014 |title=Keeping the Wild: Against the Domestication of Earth |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0006320714004315 |journal=[[Biological Conservation]] |volume=180 |page=288 |doi=10.1016/j.biocon.2014.11.006 |bibcode=2014BCons.180..288P |access-date=July 8, 2020|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Pimm's article "sparked debate on Twitter almost immediately."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://retractionwatch.com/2014/11/21/i-dont-take-whores-in-taxis-casual-sexism-in-scientific-journal-leads-to-editors-note/ |title="I don't take whores in taxis": Casual sexism in scientific journal leads to editor's note|last=Ferguson |first=Cat |date=October 12, 2014 |website=Retraction Watch |access-date=June 22, 2020}}</ref> Pimm defended his stance by stating that the line which had received criticism was dialogue from a movie.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ferguson |first=Cat |date=2014-11-21 |title='I don't take whores in taxis': Casual sexism in scientific journal leads to editor's note |url=https://retractionwatch.com/2014/11/21/i-dont-take-whores-in-taxis-casual-sexism-in-scientific-journal-leads-to-editors-note/ |access-date=2025-10-06 |website=Retraction Watch |language=en-US}}</ref>

The journal did issue a ''mea culpa'', indicating an opinion of Pimm's article. "We would like to inform our readers that parts of the book review ''Keeping Wild: Against the Domestication of the Earth'' by Stuart Pimm, Volume 180, pages 151–152 are denigrating to women.".<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Primack |first1=Richard |last2=Broerse |first2=Sandra |date=December 2014 |title=Editorial Note: Inappropriate language in a recent book review |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0006320714004315 |journal=[[Biological Conservation]] |volume=180 |page=288 |doi=10.1016/j.biocon.2014.11.006 |bibcode=2014BCons.180..288P |access-date=July 8, 2020|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Of Pimm's article, the journal admitted that "It just contains some offensive language." When challenged, Pimm responded that he did not think his "wording was sexist..." However, some disagreed. In a later letter to the editor,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Stanley |first1=Amanda G. |date=February 2015 |title=Response to Pimm (2014): Misogynist metaphors don't belong in scholarly discourse |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0006320714004613 |journal=[[Biological Conservation]] |volume=182 |page=13 |doi=10.1016/j.biocon.2014.11.036 |bibcode=2015BCons.182...13S |access-date=July 8, 2020|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Amanda Stanley, then Conservation Science Program Officer at the [http://www.wilburforce.org/ Wilburforce Foundation], explained why Pimm's "...book review [was] so offensive."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://retractionwatch.com/2014/11/21/i-dont-take-whores-in-taxis-casual-sexism-in-scientific-journal-leads-to-editors-note/ |title="I don't take whores in taxis": Casual sexism in scientific journal leads to editor's note |last=Ferguson |first=Cat |date=October 12, 2014 |website=Retraction Watch |access-date=June 22, 2020}}</ref> An article in ''[[The New Yorker]]'' later that year explored the debate between conservationists that led to Pimm's controversial remark. The article asserted that, in his review, "Pimm's emotions got the better of him." For his part, according to the article, Pimm was reported as being "totally unrepentant."<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.newyorker.com/tech/annals-of-technology/bridging-conservation-divide/ |title=Bridging the Conservation Divide |last=Nijhuis |first=Michelle |publisher=Condé Nast |date=December 9, 2014 |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |access-date=July 8, 2020}}</ref>

== Personal ==
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=September 2023}}
Pimm married Julia Killeffer in 1990. He has two daughters from a previous marriage, both in the United States. He lives in Durham, North Carolina in USA but travels extensively around the world.
